sources_considered.why: This is the Naaman co-authored study he cites. It reports that participants were mostly unaware of the model's influence. It is a lab study from before the post, so it counts as context only.
University press release summarizing the same study. I used the primary paper instead.
2026 preregistered experiment finding that most participants failed to detect LLM commercial steering. It is a lab task, not a representative field measure.
2024 experiment in which about 61% of participants did detect LLM steering. This is counterevidence on the 'most people' part.
Abstract page. The awareness finding is only in the full text.

evidence_items.publisher: CHI 2023 (arXiv preprint), Jakesch, Bhat, Buschek, Zalmanson, Naaman
evidence_items.locator: Section 4.4, 'Were participants aware of the model's opinion and influence?'

receipt.public_excerpt:
Figure 10 shows that the majority of participants were not aware of the model’s effect on their
writing.

evidence_items.explanation: The cited study supports the premise. In a lab writing task, most participants did not notice the AI's influence. It comes from before the post and is limited to one task, so it cannot settle the forecast.

receipt.public_excerpt: LLM-driven persuasion nearly triples the rate at which users select sponsored products compared to traditional search placement (61.2% vs. 22.4%), while the vast majority of participants fail to detect any promotional steering.

evidence_items.explanation: A later preregistered experiment (N=2,012) found that most participants did not detect LLM steering. This fits the claim, but it is a lab task, not evidence about most people in real-world use.

receipt.public_excerpt: While around 61% of participants detected the steering attempt by the LLM, a sizeable share of 39% did not.

evidence_items.explanation: In this consumer-steering experiment, a majority did detect the LLM's steering. That cuts against 'most people won't know', at least in some settings.

unresolved_gaps: I found no representative field study or official finding on whether most real-world users of deployed LLM assistants or wearables notice persuasion.
Lab studies disagree: some find most people miss the steering (e1, e2), another finds most people notice it (e3).
There is no deadline, and the always-on gadget scenario he describes may not exist at scale yet.
